goal: Lets users and external wallet software manually set and remove prune locks via RPC (setprunelock/listprunelocks) and a new -prunelockheight startup option.
Protects blocks needed for future wallet rescans on pruned nodes, and lets locks be cleaned up when no longer needed.
reviewability: Ready. Active review through September 2026 with no open mechanical blockers.
agreement: Positive with two approvals for stated reasons (sedited) and a maintainer explanation that convinced an initial skeptic (achow101, stickies-v).
A fresh usefulness objection is open but is about value not a concrete harm, so it does not block merge (andrewtoth).

categories.name: rpc
why: P2 because it adds two new RPCs plus a startup option that let pruned-node operators and external wallets manage which blocks survive pruning, a concrete pain point achow101 confirmed exists for wallet rescans.
Not P1 since no correctness or security issue is at stake and demand outside Core's own wallet is not yet demonstrated by a named external consumer.

categories.name: indexes
why: P2 because the feature extends the existing pruning/prune-lock mechanism (block storage on disk) to be externally controllable, which the category explicitly covers.
Benefit is the same rescan-protection use case as rpc; value is real but usage outside the wallet itself remains speculative.

categories.name: docs
why: Unranked because the release notes and doc note are secondary to the RPC/init feature change, not the primary subject of the PR.

categories.name: utils
why: Unranked because the -prunelockheight startup option's point is pruning/storage behavior, not generic argument-handling infrastructure.

categories.name: validation
why: Unranked because the only touch to validation-adjacent code is a getter (GetPruneLocks) that removes a friend-class access pattern without changing consensus or chainstate validity logic.

result.summary: Adds manual prune-lock management: two new RPCs (setprunelock, listprunelocks) modeled on setban/listbanned, a new -prunelockheight startup option, and a GetPruneLocks() accessor on BlockManager. It lets users and external wallets protect specific block ranges from pruning and later release them, reusing the existing internal prune-lock mechanism without persisting locks across restarts.
result.problem: On a pruned node, blocks a wallet will need for a future rescan can be pruned away while the wallet is unloaded; there is currently no way for a user or external wallet software to protect or later release specific block ranges via RPC. achow101 confirms this is a real gap both for Core's own wallet and for external wallets that use Core as a backend.

open_concerns: andrewtoth (2026-09-09) questions whether pruneblockchain + -prune=1 already achieves the same effect and finds the motivation not fully compelling; author replied 2026-09-13 with a detailed rebuttal, no further response yet.

rkrux suggested marketing/documentation should better explain use cases and a wallet-side functional test exercising the scenario; author has partially responded (added release notes, a test) but the broader marketing ask is not fully addressed.
Earlier: whether locks should eventually persist across restarts (author opted for a startup-option approach instead, still open as future work).
resolved_concerns: luke-jr's RPCResult should stay an Object for extensibility: addressed by reverting to Object per maflcko's suggestion.
bvbfan/sedited's suggestion to copy prune locks rather than hold cs_main while iterating: implemented via unordered_map copy construction.
sedited's question about the GetPruneLocks helper's purpose: explained (avoids friend-class direct access) and accepted.
rkrux's questions about missing release notes and about future-height locks: release notes added; future-height locking kept intentionally with docs added.
discussion.author_status: active, replied 2026-09-13 to the most recent open question

agreement.summary: Positive, with two full ACKs from sedited and concept support from stickies-v/achow101, but andrewtoth's recent doubt about whether the feature is needed at all remains unanswered by other reviewers.
agreement.reason: Multiple reviewers engaged substantively and the author addressed concrete code concerns (luke-jr, bvbfan, sedited, rkrux) with fixes; sedited gave two ACKs including a re-ACK after later changes. The one standing objection, from andrewtoth, is about the feature's necessity rather than a concrete harm from merging, and per the rubric that does not itself block the PR, but it is unresolved and echoes an earlier round of the same skepticism from stickies-v that was only settled by achow101's explanation.

stickies-v: 'Concept ACK. Enabling wallets to build on top of a pruned node via RPC seems enough of a use case to move this forward.'

enables: External wallet software and indexes to reliably use a pruned Bitcoin Core node as a backend by explicitly protecting needed block ranges
Follow-on discussion of a possibly-persisted prune-lock design was deferred in favor of this manual/-prunelockheight approach

categories.name: docs
categories.evidence: Only a release-notes file and doc clarifications accompany the RPC/init feature; documentation is not the primary subject of the change.
categories.rationale: Not a member: per the docs category rule, a code change that also updates its own docs belongs to its own area, not docs.

categories.name: indexes
categories.evidence: Touches block/undo storage and the pruning mechanism (blockstorage.h, GetPruneLocks), and the category explicitly covers 'block and undo file storage on disk, and pruning.'
categories.rationale: Extends the existing prune-lock system (originally added for indexes to survive IBD, per fjahr's own #21726) to be externally controllable, which achow101 says addresses a real gap for wallets and external index-like consumers on pruned nodes. Not higher because no concrete data-integrity or performance problem is fixed, and andrewtoth still questions whether the same outcome is reachable with pruneblockchain.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: Adds two new RPCs (setprunelock, listprunelocks) and matches the RPC/REST/ZMQ label; this is the PR's primary surface.
categories.rationale: New RPCs give external software fine-grained control over pruning that currently doesn't exist, addressing a stated pain point ('blocks necessary for rescanning... may be pruned' per the PR description) that achow101 and stickies-v both endorsed as a real use case. Not P1: no compatibility break, no security exposure, and demand from an actual external wallet implementer is still unconfirmed (andrewtoth's live objection, sparrow docs cited as only 'hands-off' evidence).

categories.name: utils
categories.evidence: The -prunelockheight startup option touches init.cpp argument handling, but its purpose is pruning/storage behavior specific to blockstorage, not generic settings infrastructure.
categories.rationale: Excluded per the utils rule that a settings change whose point is one area's behavior belongs to that area (here, indexes/pruning), not utils.

categories.name: validation
categories.evidence: Adds a GetPruneLocks() getter on BlockManager to replace direct friend-class access from validation.cpp, but does not change any acceptance, chainstate, or consensus logic.
categories.rationale: Excluded per the validation rule for refactors that pass through validation-adjacent files without changing validation behavior; the substantive behavior change here is about pruning/storage, covered under indexes.

uncertainties: Whether external wallet demand is real is disputed within the thread itself (andrewtoth vs achow101/stickies-v); no named external implementer has committed to using it.
Whether the eventual design should add lock persistence across restarts is left as an open question, which could still change the RPC/init surface later.
Category placement between indexes and validation for the GetPruneLocks getter is a judgment call since it touches src/node/blockstorage.h, which both hints list.
result.card: This PR adds setprunelock/listprunelocks RPCs and a -prunelockheight startup option so users and external wallet software can manually protect or release block ranges from pruning, extending Bitcoin Core's existing internal prune-lock mechanism. The problem is that a pruned node can prune blocks a wallet needs for a future rescan while that wallet is unloaded; achow101 confirms this is a real gap for both Core's wallet and external wallets using Core as a backend. Review is active and mergeable with no blockers: sedited has given two full ACKs and stickies-v/achow101 supplied concept support, though andrewtoth raised a fresh, unresolved doubt on 2026-09-09 about whether pruneblockchain already covers the same need, which the author rebutted on 2026-09-13 without further reply yet. The change spans rpc (primary surface, new RPCs) and indexes (pruning/storage mechanism it builds on); it does not substantively touch validation or utils despite adjacent file paths. No hard dependency on other PRs, though it succeeds a previously closed attempt (#19463) and conflicts trivially with an unrelated open PR (#34486).
